mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points in a quarter suggests an improving labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3pp in a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% in a month signals increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a stable monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as market uncertainty decreases.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL remained below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as broader economic demand weakens.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST decreased by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increasing nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) suggests a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as wage pressures and consumer spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases & PAYEMS increases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased and PAYEMS increased in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer confidence improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the quarters where GDPC1 increased by more than 2%.
